study.research_problem: Pagetic femoral fractures are mechanically weakened and prone to delayed union, while severe comorbidity and deformity can make recommended internal fixation impractical.
study.exact_gap: The report addresses a rare clinical decision scenario: a Japanese patient with Paget-related femoral delayed union, pin-site infection, and high operative risk in whom functional bracing was used after external fixation (S001:C01-S004:C02).
study.objective_or_hypothesis: Describe the treatment sequence and healing of one Paget-related femoral delayed union managed with functional bracing when further surgery was judged unsuitable.
study.study_design: Single-patient diagnostic and treatment timeline with plain radiography, laboratory/radionuclide support for Paget disease, six months of external fixation followed by removal for pin-site infection, six months of functional bracing, and radiographic/functional follow-up to five years (S003:C01-S003:C02).
study.sample_or_model: One 63-year-old Japanese woman with monostotic Paget disease, a displaced transverse left-femoral fracture, bowing/deformity, elevated alkaline phosphatase, multiple comorbidities, and poor operative candidacy.
comparators: Within-patient time sequence before and after functional bracing
External fixation period with nonunion and pin-site infection versus subsequent brace period
No parallel, historical matched, surgical, or alternative-treatment control
method_spine: Document diagnostic evidence and anatomical constraints.
Explain why usual internal fixation options were unsuitable.
Report initial treatment, complication, and explicit trigger for strategy change.
Provide dated radiographic and functional outcomes after the alternative treatment.
Separate observed healing from speculative vascular/mechanical mechanisms and general treatment recommendations.

verification: Radiography, alkaline phosphatase, and radionuclide uptake provide convergent diagnostic support, but histology/genetic confirmation is not reported (S003:C01).
validation: Serial radiographs at six months after bracing and five years plus walking status document this patient's course; they do not validate brace efficacy relative to surgery or natural healing (S003:C01-S003:C02).
application_prediction: Functional bracing as an option for other Paget-related delayed/nonunions or high-risk elderly patients is hypothesis-generating and requires series/comparative evidence (S004:C02-S004:C03).

primary_outcomes: After six months of external fixation, pin-site infection prompted removal and radiographs showed no healing (S003:C01).
Radiographic healing was observed six months after application of the functional brace (S003:C01-S003:C02).
At five years after injury, the fracture was described as completely healed and the patient walked with a single T-cane (S003:C01-S003:C02).
study.highest_evidence_level_reached: One-patient longitudinal observation with radiographic and functional follow-up; no comparative efficacy, biomechanical measurement, or generalizable treatment effect.

argument_map.central_claim: Functional bracing coincided with radiographic union and long-term walking recovery in one medically high-risk patient after an externally fixed Paget-related femoral fracture had not united; the case supports clinical plausibility and a decision example, not comparative efficacy or a proven vascular mechanism.
data: Diagnostic imaging/laboratory findings, treatment timeline, pin-site infection, six-month nonunion, post-brace radiographic union, and five-year follow-up (S003:C01-S003:C02).
argument_map.warrant: A clearly sequenced rare case can show that an option was feasible in one constrained setting, while treatment attribution requires controls, protocol detail, and exclusion of spontaneous/time-dependent recovery.
backing: The authors position functional bracing within biological fracture-treatment concepts and cite earlier tibial delayed-union experience (S004:C02).
argument_map.qualifier: Single unusual case in a poor surgical candidate with Paget disease and prior external-fixator complication.
rebuttals_or_boundaries: Union occurred approximately one year after injury, so time-dependent healing and prior stabilization cannot be separated from the brace effect.
No control, mechanical loading measurement, alignment metric, callus score, independent radiographic adjudication, or patient-reported outcome is provided.
Brace design, fitting, compliance, weight-bearing/rehabilitation protocol, bone-active medication, nutrition, and comorbidity management are not described.
The vascular-preservation explanation is speculative and not measured (S004:C02).
A femoral Paget case cannot establish effectiveness for nonunion generally or superiority to internal fixation/MIPO.

measured: Plain-radiographic fracture morphology/healing, serum alkaline phosphatase, radionuclide uptake, pin-site infection, treatment timing, and walking status in one patient (S003:C01-S003:C02).
inferred: The authors speculate that avoiding disruption of the fracture site preserved vascular regeneration and blood supply (S004:C02).
Healing after the treatment switch is attributed to functional bracing despite absence of a counterfactual or quantified mechanical exposure.
The case is used to suggest a viable alternative for delayed/nonunion and high-risk patients (S004:C02-S004:C03).
recommended: Report brace mechanics and adherence, weight-bearing and rehabilitation, concurrent therapies, standardized union/function outcomes, and accumulate multicentre case-series or comparative evidence.
proxy_to_outcome_bridges: Radiographic union supports structural healing but does not quantify mechanical strength or reinjury risk.
Walking with a cane is a functional observation, not a validated patient-reported or performance outcome.
A temporal before/after sequence is not a controlled treatment effect.
A successful rare case does not estimate success rate, indication, or relative benefit.
overclaim_risks: 'Successful' is accurate descriptively for this patient's observed course but should not imply brace efficacy beyond the case (S001:C01; S004:C03).
Calling bracing a viable alternative for Paget delayed/nonunion generalizes from n=1 and unmeasured co-interventions (S004:C02).
The biological blood-supply mechanism is explicitly speculation, not a measured finding (S004:C02).
Automated finite-element and experimental-mechanical cues are false; no model or mechanical test was performed.

section_moves.execution: Diagnosis, operative risk, external fixation, infection/removal, six-month nonunion, brace initiation, union, and five-year status are presented in sequence (S003:C01-S003:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: For case reports, align each decision with its diagnostic evidence, constraint, trigger, intervention, and dated outcome so the reader can reconstruct the reasoning.

section_moves.move: Distinguish observed outcome from mechanism speculation
section_moves.execution: The paper reports union, then uses 'we speculate' for preserved blood supply (S004:C02).
section_moves.transferable_principle: State the observed change first; label the proposed biomechanical/biological explanation as a hypothesis and name the measurement needed to test it.
section_moves.failure_mode: Temporal association does not prove the proposed vascular or mechanical mechanism.

section_moves.move: Bound the transferable lesson to the constrained indication
section_moves.execution: The suggested role is framed around elderly or high-risk patients in whom major corrective surgery is unsuitable (S004:C02-S004:C03).
section_moves.transferable_principle: In rare cases, separate the reusable decision principle from any unestimated treatment effect and specify the patient constraints that made the option reasonable.
section_moves.failure_mode: A feasible rescue in one contraindicated patient is not a general standard of care.

reader_identified: Single patient, no counterfactual, and approximately one year total healing time make treatment attribution uncertain.
Sparse treatment detail: brace construction, alignment, compliance, weight-bearing, physiotherapy, medication, metabolic management, and imaging adjudication are absent.
No mechanical strength, callus scoring, limb alignment, pain, range-of-motion, validated functional, or quality-of-life outcomes.
Prior external fixation and infection are major history effects; spontaneous or delayed healing cannot be excluded.
Rare monostotic Paget disease and severe comorbidity sharply limit external validity.
likely_bias_direction: Publication of an unusual successful case favors a positive feasibility narrative.
Temporal attribution likely exaggerates the brace-specific effect and vascular mechanism.
Sparse negative/functional detail may overstate completeness of recovery.
limitations.scope_boundary: The report documents one radiographically healed Paget-related femoral delayed union after functional bracing in a poor surgical candidate. It does not establish efficacy, mechanism, comparative benefit, or a general indication.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Write rare orthopedic case reports as an auditable timeline linking diagnostic evidence, treatment constraint, failure/complication, decision trigger, and dated outcomes.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Case presentation, clinical reasoning, and figure timeline.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: A well-documented time sequence remains observational and cannot estimate comparative efficacy.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Separate a measured clinical outcome from an unmeasured biological or mechanical rationale using explicit hypothesis language.
writing_capability_candidates.manuscript_use: Discussion mechanism paragraph and conclusion audit.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Union after bracing does not prove preserved vascularity or an optimal mechanical environment.

writing_capability_candidates.capability: Extract a bounded decision principle from a single case without converting feasibility into a treatment recommendation.
writing_capability_candidates.counterexample_or_boundary: Use in one high-risk patient does not establish success rate or superiority over fixation alternatives.

critical_weaknesses: Single uncontrolled timeline with sparse treatment detail.
Mechanism and brace-specific attribution are unmeasured.
No standardized mechanical or functional outcomes.

summary_zh: 这是一篇标准的罕见病例时间线，而不是力学实验。患者因 Paget 病发生股骨病理性骨折，外固定 6 个月后因针道感染拆除且仍未愈合；随后使用功能支具，6 个月影像显示愈合，5 年时骨折完全愈合并持杖行走。可迁移的写作能力是把诊断证据、手术禁忌、初始治疗、并发症、改策触发点和带时间戳的结局串成一条可审计链。证据边界同样清楚：n=1、总病程约一年、无对照且未报告支具力学/依从性/康复和并用治疗，因此只能写‘在该病例中可行并伴随愈合’；作者提出的血供保护机制应保留为推测，也不能据此得出普遍疗效或与内固定的优劣。
reader_notes: Primary Codex reader reviewed every non-reference packet section.
The finite-element and experimental-mechanical cues are false; the brace rationale is not a measured mechanics study.
This paper is valuable mainly as a case-writing and causal-boundary exemplar.
